subject: Clarifying MSA + Order Form redlines: commercialization carveouts, telemetry & training use
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta@heliolabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@heliolabs.com
Date: Sun, 14 Jul 2029 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines (Helio)

Hi Jonas —

Attached are Helio Labs' redlines to the MSA and the order form. High level: the business team is fine with the commercial terms but legal has three sticking points we need to resolve before procurement can proceed:

1) Output ownership / productization: they want an explicit assignment for outputs derived from Helio customer data when used to productize Helio offerings.
2) Training / model use: they want stricter limits on using Helio data for model training and an opt-in mechanism if Redwood intends to retrain public models.
3) Telemetry & retention: specifics on what telemetry Redwood retains (latency/cost/trace) and how long Helio PII-free telemetry will be stored.

Please confirm a single point of contact on your side for legal + ops, and whether your team can provide suggested language for the three items above.

Attachments: Helio_MSARedline_20290714.pdf, Helio_OrderForm_Redline_20290714.xlsx

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Head of Legal Operations
Helio Labs

--
This email and any attachments are confidential.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@heliolabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2029 08:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (Helio)

Marta —

Thanks for sending the redlines and the clear summary. I'll be the point person from Redwood for contract coordination. Appreciate the three flagged areas — below is how we'd like to tackle them and a proposed next step:

- Output/productization: Redwood's standard approach is to grant customers ownership of their Customer Content and a nonexclusive license back to Redwood for service operations, while explicitly excluding derivative productization that uses customer-specific confidential information without express assignment. We can propose language that: (a) confirms Helio owns Customer Content and generated outputs, but (b) allows Redwood to use aggregated/non-identifiable outputs to improve platform models unless Helio opts out.

- Training/model use: We agree an opt-in is reasonable for model-retraining when it includes Helio confidential data. We typically offer an explicit opt-in per environment (e.g., production vs. sandbox) and the ability to scope which data sets are eligible.

- Telemetry & retention: Redwood retains operational telemetry (latency, error rates, per-request token counts) for troubleshooting and billing. We can propose a 90-day default retention for detailed traces and a longer-term aggregated storage for 2 years unless contractual SLAs require otherwise. PII is excluded by default.

Next steps: Laura (legal) will draft suggested redline language for the MSA and a short order-form amendment for the opt-in checkbox and telemetry retention. Karthik (solutions) will prepare a one-pager describing the operational implications for Helio's security and engineering teams. Could we set a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk through the language? Proposed time: Tue Jul 16 10:00 AM PT.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Head of Legal Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2029 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Draft redlines for output ownership & training opt-in

Marta / Jonas —

Per Jonas' note, attaching proposed redline snippets below (pasted) to accelerate legal review. These are intentionally concise so Helio's counsel can respond quickly. If helpful we can also provide a clean clause to drop into the MSA.

1) Output ownership (proposed):
"Customer Content" means data, text, prompts, and files submitted by Customer. Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Content and Generated Output. "Generated Output" means content produced by the Service in response to Customer Content. Redwood may use Aggregated Non-Identifiable Output for model improvements, provided no Customer Confidential Information is included.

2) Training opt-in (proposed Order Form amendment):
Add checkbox: "Customer consents to Redwood using Customer Content and/or Generated Output to improve Redwood models and services (opt-in)." Default: unchecked. Any opt-in will be documented per Order Form and scoped by environment and time window.

3) Telemetry & retention (proposed):
Operational telemetry (latency, per-request token counts, error traces) is retained for 90 days in identifiable form for support and billing; aggregated telemetry may be retained for up to 24 months. Customer PII is not retained in telemetry.

Open items for Helio to confirm: (a) whether the business requires assignment (vs. license) for Generated Output used directly in Helio product features, and (b) what retention maximum Helio requires for aggregated telemetry.

Jonas, Karthik — can you attach the one-pager on ops implications before the call? Marta — can you confirm Tue Jul 16 10:00 AM PT or propose an alternate?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Marta / team —

Thanks — quick operational notes that may help Helio's security and procurement teams evaluate risk:

- If Helio requires assignment of Generated Output for productization, there are two practical paths: (1) assignment limited to customer-specific models/features built from Helio data (i.e., a scoped assignment tied to the Order Form), or (2) assignment of outputs broadly which prevents Redwood from using those outputs to improve platform models. Path (1) is far more typical and keeps model improvement options open for Redwood while giving Helio exclusivity on productized features.

- For training opt-ins: we can implement environment-scoped checkboxes (e.g., production opt-out by default, sandbox opt-in for testing) which is usually enough for enterprises worried about inadvertent retraining. The Order Form amendment Laura suggested aligns to that approach.

- Telemetry: Redwood can offer a longer retention for aggregated telemetry (e.g., 24 months) if Helio needs it for analytics, but we recommend 90 days for detailed traces to limit exposure. Also willing to add contractual language that telemetry will exclude payload content and any fields Helio identifies as sensitive.

I'll attach the one-pager to the calendar invite. If helpful I can join the call to cover the engineering implications and the feature gating for opt-ins.

—Karthik
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas, Laura and Karthik —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear proposed language. A few clarifications from Helio legal / procurement before the call:

- On assignment vs. license: business stakeholders want the option to productize outputs without restrictions. Legal prefers assignment for any Generated Output that directly incorporates Helio Confidential Information. Would Redwood accept a scoped assignment limited to features specified in an Order Form (i.e., assignment of outputs used in a named product/feature)? That would be an acceptable compromise to both sides.

- Training opt-in: Helio will likely opt out of any automatic retraining unless explicitly scoped and listed in the Order Form. The checkbox approach is good; can Redwood add a short audit trail requirement (e.g., DocuSign/Order Form record) to show Helio's explicit opt-in?

- Telemetry: Helio requests confirmation that aggregated telemetry retained beyond 90 days will not contain any identifiers and that Redwood will provide a quarterly report summarizing telemetry access and retention.

We can keep the call short and use it to confirm these points and sign off on the redline snippets if acceptable. Tue Jul 16 10:00 AM PT works for our team.

Thanks,
Marta

--
Marta Lopez
Head of Legal Operations
Helio Labs
